title: ProMo3D: Probing Motion Cues in Frozen 3D Foundation Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.33802v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Feed-forward 3D foundation models have recently reshaped multi-view reconstruction, yet dynamic 4D understanding still often relies on large-scale motion supervision or hand-crafted, architecture-specific heuristics. We ask whether frozen 3D foundation model tokens already encode motion-relevant information that can be exposed by lightweight readout functions, rather than re-learning motion-specific features with high-capacity decoders. Through probing on three representative backbones, we find that static--dynamic separation is decodable from frozen token representations. Our rank-restricted and spectral analyses on $\pi^3$X reveal that the recovered motion cues are concentrated in a low-dimensional subspace. Building on this, we propose Probing-based Motion Distillation (PMD), which converts pairwise motion-state compatibility scores against a fixed anchor token into dense motion masks. translated_title: ProMo3D：在冻结的3D基础模型中探测运动线索
translated_abstract: 前馈式3D基础模型最近重塑了多视角重建领域，但动态4D理解仍然通常依赖于大规模的运动监督或手工设计的、与特定架构绑定的启发式方法。我们提出疑问：冻结的3D基础模型的token是否已经编码了与运动相关的信息，从而可以通过轻量级的读出函数将其揭示出来，而无需使用高容量的解码器重新学习运动特定特征。通过对三个代表性骨干网络的探测实验，我们发现静态-动态分离信息可以从冻结的token表示中解码出来。我们对π³X进行的秩受限分析和谱分析表明，恢复出的运动线索集中在一个低维子空间中。基于这一发现，我们提出了基于探测的运动蒸馏方法，该方法将相对于固定锚点token的成对运动状态兼容性分数转换为密集的运动掩码。仅使用160个YouTube-VOS视频进行训练，并采用（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文发现冻结的3D基础模型的token表示中已编码可解码的运动线索且集中于低维子空间，进而提出基于探测的运动蒸馏（PMD）方法，仅需160个视频训练即可将成对运动状态兼容性分数转换为密集运动掩码，从而无需大规模运动监督即可实现动态4D理解。
en_tdlr: This paper discovers that frozen 3D foundation model tokens already encode decodable motion cues concentrated in a low-dimensional subspace, and proposes Probing-based Motion Distillation (PMD), which converts pairwise motion-state compatibility scores against a fixed anchor token into dense motion masks with training on only 160 videos, enabling dynamic 4D understanding without large-scale motion supervision.
